aspects.name: Chatbot and microservices architecture
aspects.digest: 2024-03-01: Planned a multilingual assistant with React 18.2, Node.js 18, GPT-4 API v2024-02, and language detection, PostgreSQL 14 memory, and chatbot services on ports 3000/4000/5000; implementation was not confirmed. Through March–June, explored scaling, health checks, retries/circuit breakers, queues, Redis, deployment, secure communication, gRPC discovery/load balancing, and a separate WebSocket service on 7000. These remained proposals or plans; no deployment was confirmed.

aspects.name: Database schemas, queries, and maintenance
aspects.digest: 2024-03-01: User discussed PostgreSQL 14 schemas for chatbot memory, messages, sessions, and translations; agreed to add indexes/foreign keys and run ANALYZE and VACUUM. Later topics included UUIDs, language validation, JSONB conversation data, and query tuning. By 2024-06-22, prepared statements reportedly worked well for fetching messages by user_id; advice emphasized selecting needed columns, `(user_id, created_at)` indexing, EXPLAIN ANALYZE, and VACUUM ANALYZE.

aspects.name: Unicode, localization, and multilingual UI
aspects.digest: On 2024-03-01, the user reported garbled Unicode in a React 18.2/Node.js 18 multilingual chatbot despite trying UTF-8. The assistant recommended checking HTML and JSON UTF-8 declarations, client response parsing, Express JSON handling, PostgreSQL encoding and file encodings, then testing multilingual text, special characters, and emoji. No resolution was recorded.

aspects.name: Language detection performance and testing
aspects.digest: On 2024-03-01, the user asked how to test multilingual chatbot performance. The assistant recommended testing eight languages, special characters and emojis, end-to-end handling, UTF-8, rendering, and automated plus manual tests. On 2024-03-12, advice covered privacy-compliant test data and an example Dockerized `langdetect` API (port 4000; not confirmed implemented). The user asked whether a language-update webhook returned HTTP 200; this was not verified, and the assistant proposed SSE.

aspects.name: Project planning, milestones, and status
aspects.digest: The language-detection module was first planned for release by March 15, 2024, with staged requirements, design, development, testing and deployment milestones. On March 1, the user wanted to move its deadline to March 18; the assistant proposed a testing-focused schedule, not confirmed as adopted. The user also prioritized PostgreSQL-backed memory before translation APIs and targeted DeepL API v2 by March 25. Later goals included fine-tuning by April 20, authentication and sessions by May 1, and latency optimization by June 25 (200 ms SLA); these schedules were largely proposals. On June 30,

aspects.name: user feedback
aspects.digest: 2024-03-01: The user asked how to integrate feedback loops into the chatbot project timeline. The assistant proposed gathering feedback via forms, surveys, support channels, and analytics; analyzing themes and sentiment; prioritizing by impact and effort; then repeating collection, analysis, planning, implementation, and collection. It also recommended sharing changes through updates, release notes, or feedback reports.

aspects.name: in-app feedback forms
aspects.digest: On 2024-03-01, the user asked how to set up in-app feedback forms in the React frontend of the user's chatbot. The assistant suggested creating a controlled React feedback component with a textarea and submit handler, showing and hiding it from the main app, POSTing submitted feedback as JSON to `/api/feedback`, and adding an Express endpoint to receive it and optionally store it. The user did not confirm implementing this approach.

aspects.name: PostgreSQL connection troubleshooting
aspects.digest: On 2024-03-01, the user reported Node.js 18 `pg` could not connect to PostgreSQL 14 on localhost:5432 despite apparently correct credentials; no error or resolution was given. The assistant suggested checking service, credentials, PostgreSQL config, logs, firewall/network, and Node.js error handling. When asked how to test network issues, it recommended ping, telnet, port checks, interfaces, DNS, and SELinux/AppArmor checks.

aspects.name: Corporate firewall troubleshooting
aspects.digest: On 2024-03-01, the user asked how to tell whether a corporate firewall was blocking a PostgreSQL connection. The assistant recommended consulting the organization's IT department and firewall policies or logs, testing with `telnet` or `nc` against port 5432, and trying a different network to isolate the cause. It also suggested requesting TCP port 5432 access and described SSH local port forwarding and PostgreSQL external-listening configuration as possible approaches.

aspects.name: Rate limiting, retries, and resilience
aspects.digest: Rate-limit resilience first came up on 2024-03-01: advice included exponential backoff, jitter, bounded retries, throttling/queues, circuit breakers, and checking `Retry-After`; no implementation was confirmed. Through March–June, examples covered OpenAI/DeepL retries, queueing, circuit breakers, and fallbacks, with retry limits varying (often 3–5). On 2024-06-22, the latest state included proposed five-response caches for chatbot outages and a three-attempt, 10-second retry example that did not implement circuit-breaker state.

aspects.name: Language detection and identification
aspects.digest: Language detection first arose on 2024-03-01, with an Express/OpenAI GPT-4 proposal and a 95% accuracy goal by March 10; neither a verified GPT-4 implementation nor meeting the goal was confirmed. The user compared franc v6.1.0 and langdetect v1.0.1; the assistant favored franc for Node.js integration, but no final choice was recorded. By 2024-03-12, the user reported franc at 93% test accuracy, alongside detection errors and performance work. They added a proposed English fallback below confidence 0.6; implementation and improvement were unconfirmed. On 2024-03-26, short-text misidentificatio

aspects.name: Docker, Kubernetes, and deployment
aspects.digest: 2024-03-01: Asked about Kubernetes horizontal scaling; examples covered Minikube/EKS, three-replica Deployments and HPAs, but no setup was confirmed. Docker image-size work followed: chatbot target under 150 MB, then language-detection image reported at 120 MB; multi-stage Node 18 Alpine builds were suggested. 2024-03-26: Planned production deployment of merged translation service via Docker Compose. Apr–Jun: explored microservices, CI/CD, Kubernetes and AWS ECS/Fargate, including autoscaling, rolling/blue-green deployments, App Mesh and GitHub Actions. Last state (2024-07): planned to deploy

aspects.name: Redis and caching
aspects.digest: Redis caching first came up 2024-03-01 for chatbot context and API load; TTLs, cache-aside, invalidation and local-memory alternatives were discussed, not confirmed. By 2024-03-12, language-result caching reportedly cut DB load 40%; later, translation caching cut API calls 30% (2024-03-26). Permission-cache hit rate reached 80%, DB load fell 35% (2024-04-30); chatbot LRU hit rate reached 92% (2024-06-22). Latest: user asked how to set up Redis in the Node.js backend; no setup decision recorded.

aspects.name: Problem-solving and response preferences
aspects.digest: On 2024-03-01, the user said complex coding tasks are hard to approach methodically and asked for clear expectations and a four-stage framework: define, gather, analyze, develop. They value fallback strategies for API errors, deadlines, TypeScript type safety, and cache hit-rate statistics; on 2024-04-30, they requested token-expiry durations in all authentication-token guidance. By 2024-06-22, priorities included reducing GitHub Actions/Docker runs from 15 to 7 minutes, maintaining high uptime and zero-downtime deployment, and optimizing latency and performance.

aspects.name: API design, integration, and error handling
aspects.digest: 2024-03-01: Planned Node.js APIs targeting <300 ms; discussed async DB/API handling, REST endpoints, production errors, and TLS 1.3. 2024-03-12–26: Fixed a language-detection 404 (GET vs POST); planned translation routes and DeepL integration, with custom errors, fallbacks, and a circuit breaker. 2024-04–05: Latency fell 350→280 ms; later memory-store latency remained high. 2024-05–06: Troubleshot latency and planned webhooks. 2024-06-22: Discussed streaming and API-change resilience; approved JSON parsing, Winston logging, sessionId validation, and error handling for the session-end webhook.

aspects.name: Contextual memory and conversation storage
aspects.digest: Contextual memory storage first came up on 2024-03-01 with JavaScript state keyed by user ID; no implementation was confirmed. On 2024-03-12, discussion covered prompt history and Redis lists. On 2024-03-26, the user explored Node.js/PostgreSQL schemas, JSONB history and real-time updates. By 2024-04-05, the focus was PostgreSQL 14 JSONB state, atomic current/history updates, indexing, caching and API performance. The roadmap later listed implementation by 2024-04-10; completion was not confirmed.

aspects.name: Chat interface and frontend behavior
aspects.digest: On 2024-03-01, the user began building a React multilingual chat UI with language selection, message history, and sending; recommendations included local state, fetching history, and considering localization libraries, but adoption was not confirmed. On 2024-03-12, focus shifted to per-message language badges, automatic language switching, and responsive badge styling. On 2024-03-26, the user added auto-translation, default off, and asked about saving preferences; local storage or backend sync were suggested. On 2024-04-05, topics included local-time timestamps, WCAG accessibility, toggle ARIA

aspects.name: Authentication, JWT, and authorization
aspects.digest: JWT security first came up 2024-03-01: one-hour tokens, verification, expiry and revocation were discussed; no production design was confirmed. By 2024-03-12, refresh tokens (7 days) were proposed. In April–May, work expanded to RS256, React refresh flows, and role/permission-based access in Flask/Express, with varied expiry targets (15 min–3 hours). Redis token storage was discussed 2024-05-12; implementation remained unconfirmed.

aspects.name: Logging, monitoring, and operational readiness
aspects.digest: 2024-03-01: Planned Winston 3.8/Node 18 logging; recommendations covered structured logs, rotation, aggregation, alerts and Prometheus/Grafana, with no tool selected. Mar–Apr: explored GPT-4 metrics, training monitoring/tuning, and fine-tuning completion notifications; no decisions recorded. 2024-05-28: sought centralized encryption-service logs and 99.9% uptime; sample load results were all HTTP 200. 2024-06-22: investigated correlation IDs and X-Ray tracing; endorsed logged segment IDs and configurable LOG_LEVEL (INFO default). Also asked about ECS autoscaling alarms; no choice recorded.

aspects.name: Git, CI/CD, and release process
aspects.digest: Git and CI/CD first came up on 2024-03-01: the user was initializing a chatbot repository and exploring GitHub Actions. By 2024-03-12, they were merging `feature/lang-detect` and wanted Prettier run before commits. On 2024-04-05, they reported tagging v0.3.0; later work covered feature-branch merges, CI, Docker builds and AWS ECS deployment. On 2024-06-08, they reported Slack failure alerts and release v0.6.0. By 2024-06-22, deployment time was 15 minutes; they wanted 7, and asked about a documented v1.0.0 release. Suggestions throughout were not necessarily adopted.

aspects.name: API performance, latency, and profiling
aspects.digest: 2024-03-01: Asked about reducing GPT-4 API latency, rate limits, and detailed profiling metrics; async calls and timing examples were suggestions, not verified implementations. In March, reported language-detection latency of 100–180 ms and translation latency of 180–220 ms; explored profiling, caching, batching, and load testing. By March 26, reported translation latency of 180 ms and Redis hit rate of 85%; no measured webhook improvement was reported. Later sought a 200 ms chatbot SLA and investigated latency, CPU, memory, and event-loop bottlenecks. By June 22, used console timing and prom-

aspects.name: Testing, debugging, and code review
aspects.digest: Testing/debugging first arose Mar 1, 2024: ESLint `bar` scope and Vite/React setup issues. Mar 12–Apr 5 brought React Router, HTTP 500 and PostgreSQL/Docker debugging; no root causes were confirmed. Apr 30 auth tests reached 92% coverage. May 10–15 sprint plan prioritized auth; May 12, 2% of 120 integration tests failed with 401s. Jun 22, PR tests with 95% coverage intermittently hit “socket hang up”; mocking external calls was suggested.

aspects.name: Memory store implementation
aspects.digest: On March 1, 2024, the user said they were prioritizing implementing a PostgreSQL memory store before integrating translation APIs. The proposed `memories` table had `id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY`, `user_id INTEGER NOT NULL`, `memory TEXT NOT NULL`, `created_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`, and `language VARCHAR(2) NOT NULL`. The user reported a database error saying the `language` column was too small and asked how to fix it.

aspects.name: Translation services and integration
aspects.digest: Translation services first came up Mar 1, 2024: Google Translate v3 was favored for coverage and cost; DeepL v2 for European-language quality. On Mar 12 the user chose DeepL, citing 15% lower latency, and planned a scalable Node/Express microservice on port 4500. Through Mar 26, discussion covered integration, errors and fallback, security, HTTPS/TLS, Docker networking, caching, and webhooks; implementation was not consistently confirmed. By Apr 5, `/api/translate` used Redis (60-second TTL) before DeepL, and the user sought better performance at about 200 concurrent requests.

aspects.name: Redis cache and database queries
aspects.digest: On 2024-03-12, the user asked how Redis could reduce database queries and shared Python code using `LINDEX` on a per-user list before a simulated database lookup. The assistant recommended cache-aside: check Redis, fetch on a miss, then cache with `RPUSH` and `LTRIM`, retaining up to 10 messages.

aspects.name: Webhook, SSE, and real-time updates
aspects.digest: Webhook/SSE discussion began Mar 12, 2024: proposed Express examples separated JSON endpoints from SSE streaming, but no implementation or HTTP 200 was confirmed; CORS was recommended. Mar 26, Grafana alerts were suggested. Apr 5, a JWT-authenticated endpoint to update session `last_active` was proposed. Apr 18, Redis logout-cache invalidation tests were discussed. Apr 30, the user reported a logout webhook problem; advice included JSON parsing, HMAC verification, logging, and curl/Postman testing. No fix was confirmed.

aspects.name: React lazy loading
aspects.digest:
React lazy loading first came up on 2024-03-26: the user had updated the chat UI to React 18.2 and used React.lazy with Suspense to load `TranslationToggle` from `./TranslationToggle`, with a `
Loading...
` fallback; it was causing issues, and they requested a code review. On 2024-06-22, they asked how to implement component lazy loading to improve performance.

aspects.name: lazy-loading error handling
aspects.digest: On 2024-03-26, the assistant suggested adding an error boundary, testing under slow network conditions, and checking code splitting and bundle output for the user's lazy-loaded TranslationToggle. The assistant supplied a function-component example that used useState and a handleError function as an error boundary; this was the assistant's proposed code, not a confirmed implementation by the user.

aspects.name: Webpack code splitting
aspects.digest: On 2024-03-26, the user asked whether Webpack needs specific configuration for React.lazy and dynamic imports. The assistant recommended dynamic-import/code-splitting support, content-hashed output and chunk filenames, runtimeChunk: 'single', and a splitChunks vendor cache group; it also suggested checking network throttling and using webpack-bundle-analyzer. No user adoption of these suggestions was confirmed.

aspects.name: React Suspense setup
aspects.digest: On 2024-03-26, the user asked whether the React setup needed adjustment for Suspense to work with lazy loading. The assistant reiterated correct lazy/Suspense usage, suggested Babel presets @babel/preset-env and @babel/preset-react with babel-loader, and repeated the Webpack and error-boundary recommendations. The user did not confirm making these changes.

aspects.name: unsupported-language fallback
aspects.digest: On 2024-03-26, the user asked how to handle a preferred target language that the translation API does not support. The assistant compared falling back to English with detecting the input language again and translating to English: English fallback is simpler and generally faster, while redetection adds latency, computational overhead, and possible failure points. The assistant recommended allowing a supported secondary language, notifying users about unsupported languages, and updating the supported-language list.

aspects.name: performance and UX
aspects.digest: On March 26, 2024, the user sought practical code-review recommendations to improve chat UI responsiveness and translation-service performance, with attention to Redis caching, database-query optimization, latency, UI/UX, and accessibility.

aspects.name: Database schema for user preferences
aspects.digest: On 2024-03-26, the user asked whether their contextual-memory API schema needed additional tables for user preferences. The assistant recommended a PostgreSQL `user_preferences` table with `id`, `user_id`, `preferred_language` (`CHAR(2)`), `auto_translation` (boolean defaulting to false), `created_at`, and `updated_at`, linked to `users` by a foreign key; the example did not enforce one preference row per user.

aspects.name: User-preferences API
aspects.digest: On 2024-03-26, the assistant provided example Express CRUD endpoints for creating, retrieving, updating, and deleting preference rows at `/api/user-preferences` and `/api/user-preferences/:user_id`. The examples queried PostgreSQL through `client`; there is no confirmation that the user implemented them.

aspects.name: Frontend integration of preferences
aspects.digest: On 2024-03-26, the user asked whether the frontend needed updating to fetch user preferences. The assistant recommended fetching preferences at login or app initialization, storing them in frontend state, and using them to configure the experience. Its React example fetched `/api/user-preferences/${userId}` with Axios and displayed the preferred language and auto-translation status; the assistant also mentioned Context API or Redux for larger applications. No frontend changes were confirmed as implemented.

aspects.name: Model serving, routing, and inference
aspects.digest: On 2024-03-26, the user integrated GPT-4 API v2024-02 on port 5000 and explored Locust testing at 50 concurrent users; suggested settings and tests were not confirmed. On 2024-04-18, they explored profile-based clinical/base GPT-4 routing and 503 fallback, plus clinical-mode UI updates; implementation was unconfirmed. They also reported 6.5 GB GPU use on an A100 and a memory bottleneck in PyTorch inference. Advice covered inference optimization, deployment scaling, and batch processing; no changes were confirmed.

aspects.name: chatbot load testing
aspects.digest: On 2024-03-26, the user asked how to load-test a chatbot with Locust using 100 concurrent users and measure average response time. The assistant proposed posting “Hello world” to `/api/chat` in a `ChatbotTest(HttpUser)` task, with 1–5 second waits, and running `--users 100 --spawn-rate 10`. It recommended checking average response time, requests per second, and errors in Locust’s web interface.

aspects.name: Fine-tuning datasets and model training
aspects.digest: 2024-03-01–04-20: Assistant proposed a GPT-4 clinical psychology fine-tuning roadmap; setup and data prep were marked complete, fine-tuning ongoing, evaluation and deployment planned (proposed statuses). 2024-03-26: User explored PyTorch distillation and transfer learning; no implementation confirmed. 2024-04-05: User targeted 2024-04-20, discussed settings, preprocessing 10,000 anonymized dialogues, and a Hugging Face example. 2024-04-18: User reported 12 epochs and validation loss 0.45→0.12, but also dataset-format errors; planned manual train/validation splits and reformatting. Final state:

aspects.name: JavaScript concurrency and stale context
aspects.digest: On 2024-04-05, the user reported a race condition that could cause stale context data when multiple calls to their JavaScript `sendMessage(message)` function overlapped; the function awaited `sendMessageToServer(message)`. The assistant recommended serializing sends with a promise-based lock/mutex so only one send runs at a time, releasing the lock after success or failure, and mentioned batching or more sophisticated concurrency control if serialization caused performance problems.

aspects.name: session activity tracking
aspects.digest: On 2024-04-05, the user was trying to implement a feature that updates a session's last_active timestamp on each user message in a React and Node.js application, and asked for help reviewing error handling and edge cases. The user supplied an Express POST route at /webhook/update-last-active with placeholder update logic and a try/catch.

aspects.name: session activity tracking implementation advice
aspects.digest: On 2024-04-05, the assistant proposed an Express implementation for updating user_sessions.last_active in PostgreSQL. The example parsed a Bearer JWT, verified it with jsonwebtoken, required userId and sessionId from the token, and parameterized the SQL update. It returned 401 for a missing token, 400 for missing identifiers, and 500 for database or caught errors. The assistant also showed a React/Axios request using a JWT from localStorage, suggested calling it when a user sends a message, and advised handling request errors. These were recommendations, not confirmed implementation choices.

aspects.name: Backend preference persistence
aspects.digest: On 2024-04-18, the user asked whether the backend needs configuration to handle the clinical-mode toggle. The assistant recommended GET and PUT endpoints for retrieving and updating a user's preference and persistence of a `clinicalMode` boolean. Its illustrative implementation used Express and Mongoose/MongoDB, although the user's stated stack includes PostgreSQL 14.

aspects.name: Frontend state updates
aspects.digest: On 2024-04-18, the user asked whether the frontend should reflect a clinical-mode change immediately. The assistant recommended optimistic local state updates, asynchronous persistence to the backend, and loading/error feedback, with an optional rollback if persistence fails.

aspects.name: React frontend performance and UX
aspects.digest: 2024-04-18: Reported Lighthouse 90 for a React chat UI with login/logout spinners; sought 98 and virtualized messages. Suggestions included lazy loading and `react-window`, not confirmed adopted. 2024-05-12: Reported mobile score 98; explored further optimizations, duplicate-send prevention, and profiling. 2024-06-08: Reported 1.2-second global load on S3/CloudFront and sought 60fps mobile animations. 2024-06-22: Focus shifted to skeleton loading, fetch errors/retry, perceived-wait and render measurement; said they would implement skeleton and error-handling improvements.

aspects.name: End-to-end encryption and cryptography
aspects.digest: E2EE first came up May 12, 2024, when the user sought secure chat encryption and key exchange; discussions covered AES, Diffie–Hellman/ECDH, key management, and WebSockets. On May 28, the user reported building a microservice with AES-256-GCM and DH, though implementation issues remained. On June 22, they again requested an AES-256-GCM/DH chat example. No validated E2EE design or completed implementation is confirmed.

aspects.name: Token refresh and expiration
aspects.digest: On 2024-04-30, the user asked about Axios token refresh for a chatbot API and reported fixing a race condition caused by simultaneous requests. Examples proposed adding bearer tokens, handling 401s, refreshing and retrying requests, and clearing the session or redirecting to login on failure; one used a `_retry` flag and `/refresh-token`, another queued concurrent requests and used `/token/refresh`. No implementation was confirmed.

aspects.name: Security, compliance, and network protection
aspects.digest: 2024-04-30: Asked about HSTS for a Node.js/Express HTTPS authentication service; certificate renewed Apr 25. Suggested `Strict-Transport-Security` and testing before preload. 2024-05-28: Investigated suspicious Wireshark traffic for possible MITM; no findings or plugins confirmed. User wants encryption status indicators in frontend security answers. 2024-06-15: Preparing encryption documentation for a GDPR audit. 2024-06-22: Implemented admin MFA; accepted suggestions to use AWS STS, error handling, rate limiting, and session management.

aspects.name: WebSocket and real-time chat
aspects.digest: WebSocket and real-time chat first came up on 2024-05-12: the user asked about a Node.js `ws` server, delivery status, disconnects, memory, performance, testing, security, and EKS deployment. RAM reportedly fell from 1.2 GB to 800 MB, then to 750 MB under typical load; the service used port 7000 and Redis. The assistant offered monitoring, reconnection, scaling, and optimization advice, but implementation was not confirmed. On 2024-06-08, the user asked how to refresh a React Query chat UI on new messages; the assistant recommended invalidating the query when a WebSocket message arrives.

aspects.name: System performance and memory management
aspects.digest: On 2024-06-08, the user had set Node.js heap size to 512 MB per service and asked how to monitor and optimize it. The assistant recommended memory metrics, profiling, leak prevention and `--max-old-space-size=512`, cautioning against frequent forced GC. On 2024-06-22, the user reported memory-leak warnings in the memory store after GC tuning and worried about user/session management. The assistant suggested heap-snapshot comparisons, investigating retained references, and testing with GC and a 4096 MB heap limit. No leak cause or fix was confirmed.

aspects.name: LLM API integration and streaming
aspects.digest: On 2024-06-08, the user explored integrating GPT-4 streaming into Node.js to reduce perceived latency. The example used the hypothetical `gpt-4-api` package, `GPT4API`, `api.stream` with `maxTokens: 1024` and `temperature: 0.7`, then `for await` to log chunks. On 2024-06-22, they asked whether to follow GPT-5 updates; the recommendation was to start immediately.

aspects.name: CDN and static asset caching
aspects.digest: The user showed a client-side caching example with a `cacheTimeout` of 3600 seconds and an in-memory `cachedAssets` object. The example fetches the asset, converts the response to a blob, and stores it, but the user was unsure whether this approach was correct or whether cache invalidation or a cache hierarchy would be better.

aspects.name: Documentation, standards, and versioning
aspects.digest: First arose 2024-06-08: user wanted a project-wiki coding best-practices guide. Assistant advised PEP 8, docstrings, testing, flake8/Black, and Git; adoption wasn’t confirmed. On 2024-06-22, user asked for a Confluence architecture and deployment plan; assistant suggested pages for overview, diagrams, deployment, technical docs, and FAQs, with review and a deployment checklist.

aspects.name: MFA authentication
aspects.digest: On June 22, 2024, the user asked whether the MFA service needed configuration for different time zones. The assistant said no explicit time-zone configuration is generally needed, but server and device clocks should be synchronized because time-based one-time passwords have short validity windows; it also suggested using consistent time handling and converting timestamps for display or logging.

aspects.name: Deployment rollback and release
aspects.digest: [2024-06-22] Discussed blue-green releases: deploy to the inactive Blue/Green environment, health-check, switch load-balancer traffic, and retain the former active environment for rollback. AWS ALB uses separate target groups and a listener change; Nginx uses separate upstreams and reload. CI/CD automation (Jenkins or GitHub Actions; context includes AWS Fargate) should test the switch and restore prior traffic on failure. Same day, the admin panel reported “Component not found” despite registration; troubleshooting covered paths, builds, dependencies, caches, runtime errors, and debugging.

aspects.name: Analytics dashboard
aspects.digest: On June 22, 2024, the user sought a Node.js/Express `/webhook` for chatbot session-end events; it logged a message and returned HTTP 200. They wanted meaningful analytics beyond logging, but selected or integrated no provider. They also expressed interest in satisfaction metrics for UI/UX; suggestions included direct feedback, session duration, task completion, FCP/TTI, Lighthouse, and Chrome DevTools. No recommendations were confirmed as implemented.

aspects.name: Chatbot model fallback and outage handling
aspects.digest: 2024-06-22: The user asked how to serve the last five chatbot responses during GPT-4 outages in a Node.js app. The assistant suggested an in-memory LRU cache or Redis, recommending a Redis list trimmed to five and returning the newest cached response on failure. It also suggested testing via a simulated-failure flag or query parameter. No approach or implementation was confirmed.

aspects.name: Authentication and session cache invalidation
aspects.digest: On 2024-06-22, the user struggled with session management in a React/Node.js admin panel, asked about timeouts, automatic re-login, and refresh failures, then reported session state was not updating: React initialized `userSession` to `null` without changing it, and `/update-session` did not modify Express session data. The assistant recommended one-hour JWTs, refresh every 30 minutes, retrying once after 401, and logging out if refresh failed; implementation was unconfirmed.

aspects.name: Microservices service discovery and reliability
aspects.digest: On June 22, 2024, the user asked how to scale an admin panel and implement AWS auto-scaling for microservices. Recommendations included stateless services, caching, load balancing, circuit breakers, queues, monitoring, and autoscaling via EC2 Auto Scaling, Elastic Beanstalk, or ECS/EKS Fargate. Example settings: 2 minimum, 10 maximum, 4 desired, 70% CPU target. No implementation was confirmed.

aspects.name: Chatbot API performance
aspects.digest: 2024-06-22: User reported chatbot API latency averaging 280 ms and aimed for 200 ms, seeking practical help, including async-call optimization. Assistant suggested profiling queries/code, caching, connection pooling, nonblocking I/O, trimming middleware, and tuning Fargate resources, autoscaling, networking, and CloudWatch/X-Ray monitoring. These were recommendations; no changes were confirmed.

aspects.name: Chatbot scaling
aspects.digest: On June 22, 2024, the user said they had scaled their chatbot API service to 5 replicas on AWS Fargate to handle increased user load during June.
